problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=\sqrt{t}-{t}^{3/2}$, where $t>0$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=\frac{4}{15}\,\text{m}/\text{s}$ when $t=1\,\text{s}$, determine the moment in time when the particle is stationary.

activity_context.topic_title: Determining Characteristics of Moving Objects Using Integration

feedback.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=(2t+1)^{3}$, where $t>0$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=\frac{65}{8}\,\text{m}/\text{s}$ when $t=1\,\text{s}$, determine the moment in time when the particle is stationary.
feedback.worked_solution:
The particle is stationary when $v=0\,\text{m}/\text{s}.$

First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (2t+1)^{3}\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{1}{8}(2t+1)^{4}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(1)=\frac{65}{8}.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{65}{8} & =\frac{1}{8}\cdot {[2(1)+1]}^{4}+C \\ \frac{65}{8} & =\frac{1}{8}\cdot (81)+C \\ C & =\frac{65}{8}-\frac{81}{8} \\ C & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=\frac{1}{8}(2t+1)^{4}-2.$

Now, we find the moments in time when $v=0\,\text{m}/\text{s}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{8}(2t+1)^{4}-2 & =0 \\ (2t+1)^{4} & =16 \\ 2t+1 & =\pm 2.\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions are $t=-\frac{3}{2}\,,\frac{1}{2}.$

Since $t>0$, we discard solution $t=-\frac{3}{2}.$ 
Therefore, the particle is stationary when $t=\frac{1}{2}\,\text{s}.$
